arxiv-2102-13456.title: Spectrum of differential operators with elliptic adjoint on a scale of localized Sobolev spaces
arxiv-2102-13456.creator: Luís Márcio Salge 1 and Éder Rítis Aragão Costa 1
arxiv-2102-13456.description: Abstract . In this paper we provide a complete study of the spectrum of a constant coefficients differential operator on a scale of localized Sobolev spaces, H l ​ o ​ c s ​ ( I ) H^{s}_{loc}(I) , which are Fréchet spaces.

arxiv-2201-07336.title: Two applications of Grunsky coefficients in the theory of univalent functions
arxiv-2201-07336.creator: Milutin Obradović, Nikola Tuneski
arxiv-2201-07336.description: Abstract . Let 𝒮 \mathcal{S} denote the class of functions f f which are analytic and univalent in the unit disk 𝔻 = { z : | z | < 1 } {\mathbb{D}}=\{z:|z|<1\} and normalized with f ⁡ ( z ) = z + ∑ n = 2 ∞ a n ​ z n f(z)=z+\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}a_{n}z^{n} .

arxiv-2209-15599.title: Descartes’s “Rule of Signs” and Poincaré’s Positivstellensatz
arxiv-2209-15599.creator: Melvyn B. Nathanson
arxiv-2209-15599.description: Abstract . This is an exposition of Poincaré’s 1883 paper, “Sur les équations algébriques,” which gives an important refinement of Descartes’s rule of signs and was a precursor of Pólya’s Positivstellensatz. 2000 Mathematics Subject Classification 11B83, 11C08, 11B75, 12D10 1.

arxiv-2210-08568.title: High-order finite-difference entropy stable schemes for two-fluid relativistic plasma flow equations
arxiv-2210-08568.creator: Deepak Bhoriya, Harish Kumar, Praveen Chandrashekar
arxiv-2210-08568.description: Abstract In this article, we propose high-order finite-difference entropy stable schemes for the two-fluid relativistic plasma flow equations. This is achieved by exploiting the structure of the equations, which consists of three independent flux components. The first two components describe the ion and electron flows, which are modeled using the relativistic hydrodynamics equation and the third component is Maxwell’s equations.

arxiv-2304-00706.title: Large deviations of reflected weakly interacting particle systems
arxiv-2304-00706.creator: Ping Chen, Rong Wei, Tusheng Zhang
arxiv-2304-00706.description: Abstract . In this paper, we prove a large deviation principle for the empirical measures of a system of weakly interacting diffusion with reflection. We adopt the weak convergence approach. To make this approach work, we show that the sequence of empirical measures of the controlled reflected system will converge to the weak solution of an associated reflected McKean–Vlasov equation.

arxiv-2305-09461.title: Sharp constants for a class of linear integral operators on higher-dimensional product spaces 0 0 footnotetext: Key words and phrases : sharp constants, linear integral, porduct spaces. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification : Primary 42B25; Secondary 42B20, 47H60, 47B47.
arxiv-2305-09461.creator: Xiang Li, Zunwei Fu, Zhongci Hang
arxiv-2305-09461.description: Abstract Abstract: In this paper, we will study a class of linear integral operators with the nonnegative kernels on higher-dimensional product spaces, the norms of the operators can be obtained by integral of the product of the kernel function and finitely many basic functions. As application, we obtain the sharp constant for linear Hilbert operator on Higher-dimensional product spaces.

arxiv-2401-04069.title: Proof of the Nernst heat theorem Preprint: English p. 1-3; Español págs. 4-6
arxiv-2401-04069.creator: José-María Martín-Olalla
arxiv-2401-04069.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by José-María Martín-Olalla. The Nernst heat theorem is probed from purely thermodynamic arguments connected with the second law of thermodynamics, and alien to the vanishing of the specific heats, or to the unattainability of the zeroth isotherm. If the proof is accepted the second law of thermodynamics would extend its applicability and the third postulate of thermodynamics would be narrowed to the fact that the entropy of a finite-density, chemically homogeneous body must not be negative.

arxiv-2405-03499.title: Physical properties and electronic structure of the two-gap superconductor V 2 Ga 5
arxiv-2405-03499.creator: P.-Y. Cheng, Mohamed Oudah, T.-L. Hung, C.-E. Hsu, C.-C. Chang, J.-Y. Haung, T.-C. Liu, C.-M. Cheng, M.-N. Ou, W.-T. Chen, L. Z. Deng, C.-C. Lee, Y.-Y. Chen, C.-N. Kuo, C.-S. Lue, Janna Machts, Kenji M. Kojima, Alannah M. Hallas, C.-L. Huang
arxiv-2405-03499.description: Abstract We present a thorough investigation of the physical properties and superconductivity of the binary intermetallic V 2 Ga 5 . Electrical resistivity and specific heat measurements show that V 2 Ga 5 enters its superconducting state below T s ​ c = T_{sc}= 3.

arxiv-2412-14114.title: Enhancing Quantum Synchronization in a driven qubit system coupled to a structured environment
arxiv-2412-14114.creator: Amir Hossein Houshmand Almani, Ali Mortezapour, Alireza Nourmandipour
arxiv-2412-14114.description: Abstract In this paper, we delve into the issue of Quantum Synchronization in a driven two-level (qubit) system situated within a structured environment. Our findings have practical implications as we discover that adding a time-dependent periodic modulation to the transition frequency of the qubit can significantly enhance quantum synchronization.

arxiv-2507-23379.title: Polarization properties of thermal accretion disk emission. I. Direct radiation
arxiv-2507-23379.creator: L. Marra, J. Podgorný, R. Taverna, G. Matt, S. Bianchi, M. Dovčiak, R. Goosmann
arxiv-2507-23379.description: Abstract The X-ray polarimetric observing window re-opening is shedding new light on our current understanding of compact accreting sources. This is true, in particular, for stellar-mass black hole sources observed in the thermally-dominated state, for which the polarization signal is expected to depend on the accretion disk inclination and the black hole spin.

arxiv-2509-19707.title: Diffusion and Flow-based Copulas: Forgetting and Remembering Dependencies
arxiv-2509-19707.creator: David Huk, Theodoros Damoulas
arxiv-2509-19707.description: Abstract Copulas are a fundamental tool for modelling multivariate dependencies in data, forming the method of choice in diverse fields and applications. However, the adoption of existing models for multimodal and high-dimensional dependencies is hindered by restrictive assumptions and poor scaling. In this work, we present methods for modelling copulas based on the principles of diffusions and flows.

arxiv-2509-20714.title: Cryptographic Backdoor for Neural Networks: Boon and Bane
arxiv-2509-20714.creator: Anh Tu Ngo, Anupam Chattopadhyay, Subhamoy Maitra
arxiv-2509-20714.description: Abstract In this paper we show that cryptographic backdoors in a neural network (NN) can be highly effective in two directions, namely mounting the attacks as well as in presenting the defenses as well. On the attack side, a carefully planted cryptographic backdoor enables powerful and invisible attack on the NN.

arxiv-2511-22544.title: Mapping Urban Air Quality from Mobile Sensors Using Spatio-Temporal Geostatistics
arxiv-2511-22544.creator: Yacine Mohamed Idir, Olivier Orfila, Vincent Judalet, Benoit Sagot, Patrice Chatellier, [0.5em] COSYS-PICS-L, Univ Gustave Eiffel, IFSTTAR, F-78000 Versailles, France
arxiv-2511-22544.description: Abstract With the advancement of technology and the arrival of miniaturized environmental sensors that offers greater performance, the idea of building mobile network sensing for air quality has quickly emerged to increase our knowledge of air pollution in urban environments.

arxiv-2602-13507.title: Benchmarking Video Foundation Models for Remote Parkinson’s Disease Screening
arxiv-2602-13507.creator: Md Saiful Islam, Ekram Hossain, Abdelrahman Abdelkader, Tariq Adnan, Fazla Rabbi Mashrur, Sooyong Park, Praveen Kumar, Qasim Sudais, Natalia Chunga, Nami Shah, Jan Freyberg, Christopher Kanan, Ruth Schneider, Ehsan Hoque
arxiv-2602-13507.description: Abstract Video-based assessments offer a scalable pathway for remote Parkinson’s disease (PD) screening. While traditional approaches rely on handcrafted features mimicking clinical scales, recent advances in video foundation models (VFMs) enable representation learning without task-specific customization. However, the comparative effectiveness of different VFM architectures across diverse clinical tasks remains poorly understood.

pmc-10618214.title: Cost effectiveness of quadrivalent influenza vaccines in the elderly population of Malaysia
pmc-10618214.creator: Syed Mohamed Aljunid, Nur Syazana Mad Tahir, Aniza Ismail, Aznida Firzah Abdul Aziz, Amirah Azzeri, S A Zafirah, Azimatun Noor Aizuddin
pmc-10618214.description: The economic burden of influenza is a significant issue within healthcare system, related to higher medical costs particularly among the elderly. Yet, influenza vaccination rates in the elderly in Malaysia were considerably low as it is not part of Malaysia’s national immunization program, with substantial mortality and morbidity consequences.

pmc-10703745.title: Antiplatelet Treatment Patterns and Outcomes for Secondary Stroke Prevention in the United Kingdom
pmc-10703745.creator: Xuejun Liu, Jenny Jiang, Danshi Li, Jay Horrow, Hiroshi Tamada, Anja Kahl, Vignesh Hariharan, Ankur Avinav, Xiaoyan Li
pmc-10703745.description: IntroductionStroke is a leading cause of death and disability worldwide. Antiplatelet therapies are recommended to reduce the risk of recurrent stroke in patients with ischemic stroke/transient ischemic attack (IS/TIA). This study evaluated outpatient antiplatelet treatment patterns and outcomes for secondary stroke prevention (SSP) among UK adults without atrial fibrillation who were hospitalized for IS/TIA.

pmc-10705057.title: Effects of Phytase Source and Dose on Its Stability during Pelleting Process under Different Conditioning Temperatures
pmc-10705057.creator: Yuming Wang, Feng Zhao, Hu Zhang, Qianyun Zhang, Wei Zhao, Renna Sa, Jingjing Xie
pmc-10705057.description: Simple SummaryPhytase activity is affected by extreme pressure and temperature during feed processing, resulting in variable residual activity and efficacy on the digestibility of phosphorus when applied to pelleted feed. The results of this study indicate that phytase from different sources has variable thermal stability when subjected to pelleting, but the dose does not influence the recovery rate of phytase.

pmc-11351185.title: Validation of the PCL-5 in Dutch trauma-exposed adults
pmc-11351185.creator: Chris M Hoeboer, Irina Karaban, Jeanet F Karchoud, Miranda Olff, Mirjam van Zuiden
pmc-11351185.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThe PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5) is an internationally widely used self-report questionnaire that can be used to screen for probable diagnosis of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Information on the psychometric properties of the Dutch PCL-5 is currently lacking.ObjectiveWe aimed to validate the Dutch PCL-5 in a sample of Dutch adults with prior (suspected) serious injury and establish the optimal cut-off for probable PTSD diagnosis herein.MethodsData for the current study were collected as part of a long-term follow-up measurement of the TraumaTIPS

pmc-11557282.title: A Glimpse Into Rarity: A Phenomenal Case of Autoimmune Retinopathy in a Young Woman
pmc-11557282.creator: Nanditha Nair, Anusha Venkatraman, Renu Magdum, Ozukhil Radhakrishnan
pmc-11557282.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Autoimmune retinopathy (AIR) is a rare retinal disorder that causes a gradual loss of vision due to autoantibodies targeting retinal antigens, leading to photoreceptor degeneration. Early diagnosis and timely intervention are critical for preserving visual function in affected patients. Over the course of a year, a 30-year-old woman had bilateral, abrupt, painless, progressive diminution of vision, nyctalopia, photopsia, and a restricted peripheral field of vision. No family history of night blindness was found.

pmc-11605749.title: A case of probable drug-induced psoriasis to dapagliflozin
pmc-11605749.creator: Simal A Qureshi, Sarah E Finch, Michelle E Pratt
pmc-11605749.description: Exposure to certain drugs can trigger new-onset psoriasis or flaring of existing psoriatic disease. The clinical presentation of drug-induced psoriasis can vary, and although there are features suggestive of drug-induced psoriasis, there are currently no standardized criteria to differentiate it from conventional psoriasis. Patients may present with localized psoriasiform plaques, or variants such as palmoplantar, nail disease, or widespread erythroderma.

pmc-11668267.title: Factors Affecting Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy (CRRT) in Patients With Septic Shock: An Analysis of a National Inpatient Sample Database
pmc-11668267.creator: Karan Yagnik, Gaurav Mohan, Apurva Ketkar, Noel Nivera, Sharon Weiner, Chandler Patton, Doantrang Du
pmc-11668267.description: Background: Septic shock is defined as sepsis with hypotension requiring vasopressors to maintain a mean arterial pressure above 65 mmHg and having a serum lactate level of more than 2 mmol/L despite adequate volume resuscitation as per the Sepsis-3 criteria.

pmc-12517717.title: The role of analytical treatment interruptions in shaping HIV-specific immunity and HIV cure
pmc-12517717.creator: Mihiri Weerasuria, James H. McMahon, Sharon R. Lewin, Jillian S.Y. Lau
pmc-12517717.description: Purpose of reviewWhile existing guidance supports the use of analytical treatment interruptions (ATIs) in HIV cure clinical trials, their design must be tailored to the intervention and scientific question. As immunologically based cure strategies gain prominence, understanding how ATIs interact with HIV-specific immune responses is critical for their safe and effective implementation.

pmc-13194128.title: Cellular mechanisms underlying social regulation of the posterior tubercular nucleus in zebrafish (Danio rerio)
pmc-13194128.creator: Carrie L. Adams, Emily M. Scott, Fadi A. Issa
pmc-13194128.description: Social status profoundly influences animal behavior through neural plasticity, yet the cellular mechanisms that mediate reconfiguration of neuromodulatory systems remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated status-dependent structural changes in the posterior tubercular nucleus (PTN) of adult zebrafish. Animals were assigned to four social conditions: communal, isolated, dominant, or subordinate.

pmc-13244036.title: From Transseptal Puncture to Mitral Commissurotomy: A Zero-Wire-Exchange Approach Using Inoue Balloon
pmc-13244036.creator: Hossameldin Hussein, Ahmed Elsherif, Anwar Hussain, Sagar N Doshi, Adnan Nadir
pmc-13244036.description: Percutaneous mitral commissurotomy (PMC) remains the standard therapy for rheumatic mitral stenosis, although decreasing disease prevalence in developed countries has reduced operator familiarity. Advancing the Inoue balloon across the mitral valve continues to pose a technically demanding step that may extend procedures or result in unsuccessful attempts.

pmc-13282302.title: Outcomes in laparoscopic versus robotic-assisted surgery for median arcuate ligament syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13282302.creator: Zahra Arabi, Georgios Geropoulos, Pasan Jayawardena, Seiver Karim, Lillian Reza, Nicola Colucci, Vanash Patel

pmc-13555794.title: Anatomical Feature of Nasal Cavity for Endoscopic Endonasal Skull Base Surgery in Patients With GHoma
pmc-13555794.creator: Tomoharu Suzuki, Noritaka Komune, Yusuke Miyamoto, Daisuke Kuga, Yuhei Sangatsuda, Ryota Higuchi, Yuichi Saito, Daisuke Murakami, Koji Yoshimoto, Takashi Nakagawa
pmc-13555794.description: BackgroundEndoscopic endonasal skull base surgery (EESS) is widely performed for pituitary tumors. In growth hormone–secreting adenomas (GHomas), the procedure is technically more demanding than for other pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (PitNET) subtypes due to restricted instrument maneuverability. Few studies have evaluated the influence of nasal cavity morphology on this difficulty.
